item.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.36218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The beta decay of neutron-rich nuclei probes the microscopic nature of weak interactions in the nuclear medium under extreme conditions. Such weak decays drive the synthesis of heavy elements in astrophysical environments, but remain poorly understood. Far from stability, experimental data are scarce, placing strong demands on ab initio nuclear theory. Two-body weak currents have been proposed as the dominant mechanism responsible for the universal quenching of theoretically predicted Gamow-Teller decay strength. However, direct experimental validation in neutron-rich nuclei has been lacking. Here we measure the beta decay of 54K, a nucleus at the experimental frontier of radioactive ion-beam facilities. In this work, the doubly magic nature of the daughter nucleus 54Ca results in a remarkably simple decay pattern, dominated by a single transition to a neutron-unbound state at 6.2 MeV with a comparative partial half-life logft=4.4(1) or Gamow-Teller decay strength B(GT)=0.26 (+0.08) (-0.04). Our measurement is reproduced by new state-of-the-art calculations of the decay, providing direct evidence for the essential role of two-body currents in nuclear beta decay for systems with a significant neutron excess. We establish a key benchmark for theoretical predictions of weak processes in exotic nuclei.

item.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda$ elliptic flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.36237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The first measurement of the elliptic-flow coefficient ($v_{2}$) of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ hadrons performed in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV with the ALICE detector is presented as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) in central and semi-central collisions. For the $\phi$ meson, in particular, this is the first measurement of the elliptic flow in a small collision system. At low $p_{\rm T}$, a characteristic mass ordering of $v_{2}$ is observed, consistent with collective expansion of the system, in which heavier hadrons are shifted to higher $p_{\rm T}$ by a common velocity field. At intermediate $p_{\rm T}$, above 3 GeV/$c$, a baryon$-$meson splitting with a $10\sigma$ significance emerges, with the $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ baryon exhibiting larger $v_{2}$ values than mesons, while, despite its mass being close to the mass of the $\Lambda$, the $\phi$ follows the K$^{0}_{\rm S}$. The $\phi$ meson behavior disfavors a purely mass-driven interpretation of the observed patterns and supports the role of hadronization via quark recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium. These results provide complementary evidence that key signatures of partonic collectivity observed in Pb$-$Pb collisions persist in light nucleus$-$nucleus systems.
item.dc:creator: ALICE Collaboration

item.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-$\Lambda$ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
item.description: arXiv:2610.36307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent measurements of event-by-event correlations between the antideuteron and antiproton numbers in Pb$-$Pb collisions at the LHC deviate from the statistical hadronization model parameterizations that describe the yields and fluctuations of light-flavored hadrons. This discrepancy may stem from nucleosynthesis processes involved in the formation of composite states like antideuterons. In this letter, we present the first measurement of the antideuteron$-$net-$\Lambda$ number correlation obtained in Pb$-$Pb collisions with the ALICE detector. This quantity is mostly sensitive to the quantum-number correlations induced by the hadronization process, as $\Lambda$ hyperons are not constituents of antideuterons. Both the antideuteron$-$net-$\Lambda$ number correlation and the normalized second-order cumulant of the net-$\Lambda$ number are well described by the statistical hadronization model implemented in Thermal-FIST. This establishes strong evidence that the antideuteron$-$antiproton correlation is driven by the nucleosynthesis processes, while the correlation between antideuterons and non-nucleonic hadrons is primarily sensitive to the hadronization mechanism.
item.dc:creator: ALICE Collaboration

item.title: Nuclear Data Evaluation Utilizing Bayesian Monte Carlo Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.36338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While the body of experimental nuclear data continues to grow at a rapid pace, significant gaps persist. The lack of evaluated experimental data is far more pronounced in charged-particle reactions which are essential to a large portion of the isotope production community for vital medical, industrial, and national security interests. In the absence of experimental and evaluated data, isotope production relies on theoretical models that may result in low yield and isotopic impurities. This work investigates model and parameter adjustments in TALYS 2.0 to establish uncertainty bands on proton-induced cross sections, highlight influential parameters in calculations, and constrain adjustments within physically defensible bounds. The EXFOR dataset for proton-induced reactions on natural copper, comprised of 24 independent cross sections, was used for iterative Bayesian model updating. Upon convergence, parameters and their uncertainties were compared against 23 cumulative cross sections from EXFOR, highlighting the limitations of generalization. Various machine learning models were leveraged to predict TALYS performance, with a small neural network showing useful ranking capabilities across several generations, suggesting the use of a surrogate approach to screening for future evaluations.

item.title: Improved nonflow control for multiparticle correlators and system-size-dependent evolution from OO to Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2610.36922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiparticle correlations of event-plane angles, known as symmetry plane correlators (SPCs), and correlations of anisotropic flow amplitudes of different harmonics, known as symmetric cumulants (SCs), help constrain the initial conditions and the transport properties of the system formed in heavy-ion collisions. Such multiparticle correlations are robust against nonflow biases in heavy-ion collisions; however, in small systems the nonflow contribution is sizeable and can distort SPCs and SCs at low multiplicity, mimicking a flow-like signal. Evidence of nuclear-geometry-induced collectivity in light-ion collisions, such as OO and Ne--Ne, has been established at the LHC. Measurements of SPCs and SCs in these systems, and their comparison to heavy-ion collisions, can therefore clarify the system-size dependence of these correlations and the strength of nonlinear mode coupling. In this work, an improved nonflow subtraction framework based on multiplicity reweighting ($\czero$) and $v_1$-estimator-based ($\cone$) scaling is validated for selected SPCs and SCs using a controlled toy model and the \textsc{Pythia~8~Angantyr} model, where collective flow is absent by construction. We find that $\cone$ provides the more reliable nonflow control and apply it to predict the SPCs and normalized SCs in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV with the \textsc{ampt} string-melting model. The results are compared with published Pb--Pb measurements from ALICE and from \textsc{ampt} as a function of midrapidity charged-particle multiplicity $\langle N_{\rm ch}\rangle(|\eta|<0.5)$, placing light- and heavy-ion systems on a common system-size axis.
item.dc:creator: Neelkamal Mallick, Suraj Prasad

item.title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
item.description: arXiv:2610.36949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: $^{99m}$Tc [t$_{1/2}$=6.0072 h, IT: 99.9963%, E_${\gamma}$=140.51 keV (89%)] is the most widely used radionuclide for SPECT imaging. It is mainly obtained from $^{99}$Mo/$^{99m}$Tc generators, with $^{99}$Mo [t$_{1/2}$=65.924 h, $\beta^{-}$:100%] produced by fission of $^{235}$U in nuclear reactors. The aging of reactors dedicated to $^{99}$Mo production and increasingly frequent maintenance shutdowns highlight the need for alternative production routes. Among accelerator-based approaches, direct production of $^{99m}$Tc from enriched $^{100}$Mo targets using low-energy proton beams is particularly promising. Within a collaboration between the Laboratory for High Energy Physics (LHEP) of the University of Bern and the Department of Nuclear and High Energy Physics of Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, we investigated $^{99m}$Tc production with medical cyclotrons. Cross sections of proton-induced reactions on solid molybdenum targets were measured to characterise the Tc radionuclides produced during irradiation and optimise production conditions. Based on these data, a proton energy of approximately 16 MeV and a highly enriched $^{100}$Mo target of about 0.5 mm thickness were identified as suitable conditions. For a 10 h irradiation, these parameters provide a calculated $^{99m}$Tc yield of approximately 1.7 GBq/$\mu$A while maintaining radionuclidic purity within European Pharmacopoeia limits. Production tests were subsequently performed to validate the measurements and demonstrate the feasibility of this production route.
item.dc:creator: Dellepiane Gaia, D'Uva Sofia, Eggimann Lars, Gottstein Alexander, Juillerat Samuel, Kasanda Eva, Mateu Isidre, Scampoli Paola, Kadenko Ihor, Braccini Saverio

item.title: Measurement of spectator fragment pseudorapidity distributions with the STAR Event Plane Detector
item.description: arXiv:2610.37447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At sufficiently low center-of-mass energies, charged particles originating from the spectator region fall within the pseudorapidity acceptance ($2.14<|\eta|<5.09$) of the STAR Event Plane Detector (EPD). Measurements of the pseudorapidity distributions of helium spectator fragments are presented for Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{_{\mathrm{NN}}}}=$ 19.6, 14.6, 11.5, 9.2, and 7.7 GeV. The helium fragment yields in each EPD ring are extracted from fits to the deposited energy spectra using convoluted Landau distributions while accounting for the contribution from singly charged particles. The effects of the EPD detection efficiency and interactions of the fragments with the STAR beam pipe are evaluated using Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations. The resulting pseudorapidity distributions are presented as a function of collision energy and collision centrality.
item.dc:creator: Balazs Korodi for the STAR Collaboration

item.title: Particle-dependent radioluminescence color response of Eu-doped CaF$_2$ associated with energy-loss density
item.description: arXiv:2610.36714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Europium-doped calcium fluoride (Eu:CaF$_2$) exhibits characteristic blue Eu$^{2+}$ and red Eu$^{3+}$ emissions. In our previous study, the Eu$^{3+}$/Eu$^{2+}$ radioluminescence intensity ratio under $\alpha$-particle irradiation was approximately twice that under X-ray irradiation. Here, we investigate the relationship between this emission ratio and energy-loss density using H, Li, C, and Ni ion beams produced by a tandem accelerator. Radioluminescence spectra were measured for each ion species, and the effective range-averaged energy-loss density was evaluated using SRIM simulations, spanning approximately 18 to 5900~keV/$\mu$m. The Eu$^{3+}$/Eu$^{2+}$ emission-intensity ratio increased systematically from H to C ions by approximately a factor of two, whereas no further systematic increase was observed for Ni ions at substantially higher energy-loss densities. Because the energy-loss density was varied mainly by changing the ion species, its effect cannot be fully separated from that of ion-specific track structure. The X-ray result, included for qualitative comparison, showed a lower emission ratio than the ion-beam measurements, although its effective energy-loss density was estimated only approximately. These results demonstrate a systematic variation in the emission color of Eu:CaF$_2$ across different ion-beam irradiation conditions and provide baseline data for future studies of wavelength-resolved particle discrimination.

item.title: Extracting the QCD speed of sound in the presence of quantum fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The equation of state of strongly interacting matter plays a %is one of the central quantities characterizing central role in characterizing quark--gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. It has recently been recognized that the QCD speed of sound is responsible for the linear correlations between the mean transverse momentum and charged-particle multiplicity in ultra-central collisions. In realistic collisions, however, this thermodynamic correlation is inevitably biased by quantum-initiated event-by-event fluctuations. In this work, we present a novel statistical framework to correct this bias by leveraging the Gaussianity condition of the quantum fluctuations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this approach can also serve as a probe of thermalization. Validated by the event-by-event hydrodynamic simulations, the extracted speed of sound in our framework is successfully consistent with the predictions from lattice QCD, from large to small collision systems.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Shan Mu, Li Yan, Xu-Guang Huang

item.title: Systematic calculations of \beta-delayed fission probabilities using a microscopic framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.37088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The process of $\beta$-delayed fission ($\beta$DF) consists of a mother nucleus $\beta$-decaying to different states of a daughter isotope, followed by fission of the latter with a probability that strongly depends on the energy of the states populated in the $\beta$ decay. Studying this process experimentally can be challenging due to the typically small $\beta$DF probabilities. The theoretical framework presented in this work was developed to globally characterise $\beta$DF probabilities. This approach uses energy density functional based models to obtain the necessary inputs for the final probabilities, which are obtained through the nuclear reaction code TALYS. Calculations were performed for all isotopes with an experimentally measured value of $\beta$DF probabilities. Following the optimisation of the theoretical framework to better reproduce known data, a global RMS deviation of about two orders of magnitude was achieved, an accuracy that can be used to identify promising cases for future experimental $\beta$DF studies.
item.dc:creator: S. Bara, T. E. Cocolios, S. Goriely, W. Ryssens, A. S\'anchez-Fern\'andez, P. Van Duppen

item.title: Probing the inner disk edge of rotating neutron stars with dipole excitations in finite nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.37394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The nuclear equation of state shapes both the structure of rapidly rotating neutron stars and the orbital motion in their surrounding spacetime. Its uncertainty affects the mass and radius at which the innermost stable circular orbit reaches the stellar surface, a condition that defines the transition between disks whose inner edge is set by the surface and those truncated by orbital instability. We quantify how measurements of the electric dipole polarizability of neutron-rich nuclei reduce the uncertainty in this transition and in the orbital properties at the disk inner edge. We compute uniformly rotating neutron stars in general relativity for a family of equations of state that systematically vary the symmetry energy, derived from relativistic energy density functionals with density-dependent point-coupling interactions. We compare the results for the full family with those for the subset consistent with the measured dipole polarizabilities of finite nuclei. The dipole polarizability constraint reduces the spread in transition mass and equatorial radius by factors of about seven to ten across the spin frequencies considered. Along this transition, it also confines the orbital frequency at the disk inner edge to a band narrower than $20$~Hz at each spin. Combined with a measured neutron-star spin, a kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillation interpreted as disk orbital motion further restricts the mass--radius region, allowing an independent mass estimate to probe the symmetry-energy constraint. The dipole response of finite nuclei thus informs both the structure of rotating neutron stars and the orbital properties of their inner accretion disks.
item.dc:creator: P. S. Koliogiannis, N. Paar

item.title: Exploring differential two-particle correlations in $\gamma p$ and low-multiplicity pp collisions using PYTHIA8
item.description: arXiv:2602.20345v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A study of two-particle differential number ($B$) and transverse momentum ($P_{2}^\mathrm{CD}$) balance functions in photon-proton ($\gamma p$) and proton-proton (pp) collisions at $\sqrt{s}=$ 5.36 TeV is presented. The analysis focuses on inclusive charged hadrons within the pseudorapidity coverage $|\eta|<2.4$ and the transverse momentum interval $0.3 < p_\mathrm{T} < 3.0$ GeV and examines their correlations in terms of relative pseudorapidity ($\Delta\eta$) and relative azimuthal angle ($\Delta\phi$). The correlation functions are evaluated for same- and opposite-sign pairs, and their combinations are used to extract charge-dependent (CD) and charge-independent (CI) components. The evolution of the near-side peak of the CD correlations is investigated in terms of $\Delta\eta$ and $\Delta\phi$ as a function of charged-particle multiplicity ($N_\mathrm{ch}$) for $\gamma p$ collisions and compared to pp collisions at a similar multiplicity range. A clear multiplicity dependence of the balance function width is obtained. The width is found systematically lower in $\gamma p$ events than in pp collisions. This study provides valuable information on particle correlations and production mechanisms in low-$N_\mathrm{ch}$ regimes for upcoming measurements in small systems.
item.dc:creator: Subash Chandra Behera, Dukhishyam Mallick

item.title: Photoproduction of $J/\Psi$ in peripheral Oxygen-Oxygen collisions
item.description: arXiv:2605.12123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The photoproduction of $J/\Psi$ in peripheral Oxygen - Oxygen ($OO$) collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is investigated considering distinct assumptions for the modeling of the nuclear photon flux, overlap function and dipole - proton scattering amplitude. Predictions for the associated rapidity distributions and total cross - sections are presented. Our results indicate that the experimental study of the photoproduction of $J/\Psi$ in peripheral $OO$ collisions is, in principle, feasible. In addition, they point out that the combination of the results for this final state in $OO$ collisions with those obtained for $PbPb$ collisions will allow us to derive important constraints on the description of photon - induced process at peripheral collisions.
item.dc:creator: Pedro E. A. da Costa, Andr\'e V. Giannini, Victor P. Gon\c{c}alves, Bruno D. Moreira

item.title: Dynamical Coulomb effects on charged-pion HBT-radius splitting in central Au+Au collisions at few-GeV energies
item.description: arXiv:2609.23422v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The pair transverse momentum ($k_T$) and collision-energy ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$) dependent difference between $\pi^{+}\pi^{+}$ and $\pi^{-}\pi^{-}$ femtoscopic correlations was observed by the HADES and STAR Collaborations. We investigate how much of the observed splitting can be accounted for by Coulomb dynamics in 0-10\% central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.42$-5.2 GeV. Using the UrQMD model and the CRAB programme, three transport scenarios that successively include baryon-baryon, baryon-meson, and meson-meson Coulomb interactions are considered. In a separate calculation based on the baryon-baryon reference, we reconstruct the time-dependent effective charge $Z_{\rm{eff}}(t)$ and radius $R_{\rm{eff}}(t)$ of the residual charged source and propagate each pion from its individual last strong-interaction point through the evolving field. The calculations reproduce the main $k_{T}$ and $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ dependences of the radii. Baryon--meson Coulomb interactions generate most of the additional charge splitting in the microscopic calculation. The residual-source treatment also enhances the longitudinal and sideward radius ratios relative to the reference, whereas the outward ratio changes little, and the enhancement generally decreases with increasing $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$. Within the present framework, this contribution does not fully account for the data, motivating further investigation of the charged-source geometry and its interplay with strong-interaction dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Pengcheng Li, Yongjia Wang, Qingfeng Li
